items_missed: Never got or used the customer's name — opened with 'hi there' and used 'sir' for the entire call
Never asked the moving-stressors question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?')
Never stated the hourly rate per mover per hour
Never covered what's included — gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools
Never mentioned disassembly/reassembly is included, or asked whether anything needed to come apart
No No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) mention
Clock section skipped — no 'clock starts on-site when the contract opens', no 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-minute prorated increments

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped. This mattered more here than on most calls: she was stretching the reservation to 5 hours specifically because of 100–150 ft walks at both ends, which is exactly the situation where consolidation and a carload cut real time off the bill
No confirmation email explained for this call — the only email mentioned was the Meet Your Mover email
No 'bolded list at the top of the email' and no 'reply with any corrections' verification ask
No hours of operation or specific contact method — only 'you can always reach out to us'
Started to ask 'so any other...' at the close and cut herself off — never landed a clean 'any other questions before I let you go?'
No school-bus/equivalents reference to make the 5-hour estimate feel concrete
Never mentioned insurance at all (No Worries or the 60¢/lb baseline)
top_strength: Best-in-call probing on access. She wasn't satisfied with a single walk-distance answer — she separated truck-to-elevator from elevator-to-door on the 4th floor, pinned down that it was 100–150 feet, and used that to justify extending the reservation. She also chased down a prior note on the property's building phase rather than ignoring it.
coaching_note: Use the customer's name — she never said it once in a 7.7-minute call, and it's the cheapest warmth lever available. Then add the Save Your Ass prep speech: she extended this move to 5 hours because of long walks at both ends, which is precisely when consolidation and a carload tip save the customer money and shorten the job.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and reassuring with a nice 'it's a good question' pickup when he asked about crew communication, but transactional overall — zero name use, and the muddled three-attempt exchange about which 'phase' of the property he lived in left the customer answering in one-word replies.
